title: Lock screen silently drops password attempts after wake or a failed try, so retries end up wrong and trigger a faillock lockout
line: A password typed on the lock screen right after a failed try is now used instead of being silently dropped, and pressing Enter on the empty field no longer counts as a failed login.
explanation: The lock screen sent every submitted password straight to the greeter, which drops a reply when no PAM prompt is pending (during the fail delay or before the worker is ready) without any feedback. The code meant to hold the password checked authenticator.pamTimeout, a property that doesn't exist, and focus moved to the unlock button until the failure came back, so keys typed meanwhile were lost and Enter resent the old text. Enter on an empty field also sent an empty password, a real PAM failure that counts towards faillock. The open MR plasma-desktop!4182 (two commits by the reporter) tracks whether a secret prompt is pending, holds a submitted password until the next prompt arrives, clears and refocuses the field on submit, and ignores empty submissions.

commits.message:
lockscreen: don't drop passwords submitted while no prompt is pending

The greeter drops a response that arrives while no PAM prompt is
pending ("Received prompt response, but no pending prompt was found!")
without telling the user. This happens when the password is submitted
before the worker is ready (e.g. right after waking from suspend) or
during the fail delay after a wrong password.

The code that was meant to hold the password in that case checks
authenticator.pamTimeout, which does not exist; kscreenlocker calls it
inPasswordDelay, and PamAuthenticators never emits inPasswordDelayChanged
either. So the password was always sent immediately and dropped.

In addition, startLogin() moves focus to the unlock button and the field
is only cleared once the failure arrives. Keys typed in the meantime are
lost and pressing Enter submits the previous password again; retyping
after a dropped submit appends to the old text. Each such attempt counts
as a failed login, which can trip pam_faillock with the correct password.

Track whether a secret prompt is pending, hold a submitted password until
the next prompt arrives (responding from the event loop, since the
greeter stores the pending prompt only after emitting the signal), and
clear and refocus the field on submit. A timer re-enables the field if no
prompt shows up.

lockscreen: don't treat Enter on an empty field as an unlock attempt

Pressing Enter on the empty password field, e.g. to wake the screen,
sends an empty password to PAM. With nullok in the stack that is a real
authentication failure and counts towards pam_faillock, so waking the
lock screen this way can use up attempts before typing anything.

Ignore empty submissions.

BUG: 528356
